no longer present in the source's latest snapshot. It was last seen on 2026-09-05.

This is not automatically a defect in the entry. A row can leave a feed because
the vendor retired the model, because it was renamed, because it was folded into
another service tier, or because this one router delisted something that is still
served elsewhere — and those are materially different facts that a reader needs
told apart. Establish which one happened from the vendor's and the feed
publisher's own sources before writing anything. If they do not settle it, say so
on the page rather than guessing: reporting `blocked` is a successful outcome and
a plausible invention is not.

vanishes is what makes the row permanently unmintable if it ever re-lists, which
is the failure `addictedtoai-javv` documents.

items.detail:
3 findings carried by reviewers against `content/blog/anthropic-enterprise-frontier-safeguards.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Fix "whenever" to "whatever" in the closing sentence of the lockout section

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-14-carry-1.md`.

The post's lockout section closes: It ends it whenever "later this fall" turns out to mean. That is ungrammatical — "whenever" takes a time, "mean" takes a thing. The fix is one word: It ends it whatever "later this fall" turns out to mean.

### Header rounds the lockout up to three months where the body says "coming up on three"

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-14-carry-2.md`.

The header reads "you have already been locked out for three months"; the body two paragraphs later reads "for coming up on three months". The body is right — Covered Models designation for Fable 5 and Mythos 5 is 9 June 2026 and the post is dated 6 September 2026, which is two months and twenty-eight days. The header is the summary line and should not be the looser of the two. "for nearly three months" fixes it and costs nothing.

### Add concept/covered-models to the EFS blog post's mentions

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-16-carry-3.md`.

content/blog/anthropic-enterprise-frontier-safeguards.md lists mentions of org/anthropic, model/anthropic-claude-fable-5 and model/anthropic-claude-fable-5-1, but not concept/covered-models, which did not exist when it was written. Backlinks are computed from mentions lists only, so the new entry ships with an empty "Appears in" rail even though the one prose page on the site about its subject is the post. Adding the id to that post's mentions is the whole fix.

### Retiring these findings

These files' presence is what puts the findings in the Pulse's derived queue. Delete the file for each finding you fixed, in the same diff as the fix — that is what removes the item, and a file left in place puts the same finding back on the next Pulse run:

- `data/carried/j-20260906-14-carry-1.md`
- `data/carried/j-20260906-14-carry-2.md`

Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Start the OpenAI blockquote where TechCrunch starts it

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-15-carry-1.md`.

The blockquote rendered as OpenAI's words opens "We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard...". I fetched the declared anchor and searched its bytes: "We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard" is MISSING; what the page carries is TechCrunch's own bridge — OpenAI's statement "stating that both OpenAI and 'the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don't look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks.'" Everything from "the larger" onward is verbatim; the two words "We and" are the post's own reconstruction of a pronoun TechCrunch elided. The meaning is identical and the primary (the X post) is unreachable, so this is not a wrong claim — but the post's own sourcing block says "Every OpenAI quotation above is TechCrunch's rendering of that post", and for two words it is not. Fix: open the blockquote at "the larger AI community" and lead in with TechCrunch's own framing ("OpenAI's statement said that both it and...").

### Anchor the five weeks of cleanup to the main burst, not to the July bursts

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-15-carry-2.md`.

The post reads "...smaller bursts on 1 and 2 July. Leitner went on deleting agent pages for five weeks after that." WinBuzzer, the cited source, says he "continued removing agent-created pages for five weeks after the main burst ended" — and the main burst ended after 22 June, not after 2 July. As written, "after that" attaches the five weeks to the July bursts and moves the end of the cleanup about ten days later than the source puts it. Fix: "for five weeks after the main burst ended."

2 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/README.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Fix the technique/ enumeration to say it is a sample, not the directory

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-25-carry-1.md`.

The ruling reads "`content/wiki/technique/` carries `low-rank-adaptation.md`, `quantization.md` and `pruning.md`, and nothing on merging". The directory holds 15 files, not 3 — also chain-of-thought-prompting, direct-preference-optimization, flash-attention, mixture-of-experts, prompt-tuning, proximal-policy-optimization, reinforcement-learning-with-verifiable-rewards, retrieval-augmented-generation, rotary-position-embedding, speculative-decoding, structured-generation and test-time-scaling. Two of the unnamed ones (DPO, PPO) are fine-tuning techniques, so the three named are not even "the fine-tuning ones". The conclusion the sentence supports is correct and I verified it separately: no entry under technique/ or concept/ covers model merging (the only "merg" substring hits are "emergent"/"emergence"). Fixing it needs three words — "carries entries such as", or naming the count — so the sentence stops reading as the directory listing it is not.

### Re-cite the frontier.mjs line numbers in the new README section against the post-merge file

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-11-carry-1.md`.

Every `lib/render/frontier.mjs` line citation in the new "What an `org` entry declares" section was computed against the file as it stood BEFORE this same diff inserted its 29-line block comment at line 50, so each is short by exactly 29 in the merged tree. Measured 2026-09-06 in this worktree at `4ebc33db7002`: `matchProviders` is at 79 (cited `:50-61`), `orgOwnDomains` at 346 (cited `:317-326`, with "the test at `:323`" now at 352), `isVendorSourced` at 358 (cited `:329-341`), `claimRank` at 373 (cited `:344-352`, and "`:340`" is now 369), the registrable-domain comment carrying the `blog.google` / `deepmind.google` example at 337-344 (cited `:309-315`), and the `renderPlayersBoard` no-filter comment at 567 (cited `:535-549`). Five of the six now land on a different function than the one named — `:329-341` for `isVendorSourced` resolves to `registrable`, `:344-352` for `claimRank` resolves to `orgOwnDomains` — which is worse than resolving to nothing in a record whose whole purpose is that the next implementer can check it against the code. The function names are given alongside every citation, so nothing is unfindable; the fix is to add 29 to each of the six frontier.mjs numbers. The citations to `pulse/lib/corpus.mjs`, `pulse/lib/mint.mjs`, `lib/changes.mjs` and `lib/schema.mjs` are unaffected and all resolve correctly, and the block comment inside `frontier.mjs` itself cites no line numbers in its own file.

3 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/concept/covered-models.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Fix the ungrammatical seam where the efs_rollout fact is transcluded

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-16-carry-1.md`.

The body reads "Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which moves the retained window into storage the customer controls, and which {{fact:concept/covered-models#efs_rollout}}". The fact's value is a full clause with its own subject — "EFS will roll out in phases beginning in fall 2026" — so the rendered sentence is "... and which EFS will roll out in phases beginning in fall 2026", which does not parse. renderFact with `inline` substitutes the raw value plus a source span (lib/facts.mjs:216), so nothing strips the subject. Dropping "which" — "... the customer controls. {{fact:concept/covered-models#efs_rollout}}" — fixes it without touching the fact.

### Restore the dropped tail of the "Certain products" quote or mark the elision

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-16-carry-2.md`.

The body quotes "Certain products built on Claude may extend the option to use ZDR with these models to their own eligible business customers under terms agreed with Anthropic." — with a full stop. The fetched page has a comma there and continues: "..., and we are working to broaden product support over time." The omission does not change what the quoted part asserts, so this is not a false claim, but the sentence is presented as ending where it does not. An ellipsis, or restoring the clause, fixes it.

### Date the Mythos availability statuses, which are literals with no entry to bind to

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-16-carry-4.md`.

The body states 'Mythos 5 and 5.1 are listed "Limited availability", reachable only by "approved partners"'. Those are slow-class status values written as literal prose. The corpus carries no model/anthropic-claude- mythos-* entry (content/wiki/model/ holds only the five fable files), so there is nothing to transclude from and the values will rot silently if Mythos goes generally available. Attributing them to the table as read on a date — "the table listed them ... on 6 September 2026" — makes the sentence dated rather than live, at one line's cost.

### Declare byteplus.com in publishes_from once the field exists

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-01-carry-1.md`.

The brief required `publishes_from`; it cannot be declared today. `entrySchema` in `lib/schema.mjs` is `.strict()` and rejects the key — measured: `entrySchema.safeParse({...entry, publishes_from: ['bytedance.com']})` returns `Unrecognized key: "publishes_from"` — and `grep publishes_from lib/` returns no matches, because the field lives only in the pending `separate-a-claim-from-a-fact` amendment. The live substitute already covers part of the ground: `orgNameTokens` in `lib/render/frontier.mjs` derives the token `bytedance` from this entry's display name, so a claim cited from `seed.bytedance.com` attributes correctly with no declaration. What it does not cover is the domain this entry itself establishes as the only place the model can be called from abroad — `ai.byteplus.com`, whose registrable label `byteplus` is not one of the org's name tokens. When the field lands, this entry needs `publishes_from: [byteplus.com]`, or a real BytePlus-hosted Seed claim renders as the honest-looking blank FM-N6 describes.

### Reconsider the bare "Seed" alias — it widens two joins that ignore alias class

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-01-carry-2.md`.

The entry declares `- name: Seed / class: manual`. `manual` correctly keeps the linker off it, but neither mechanism that reads this list looks at `class`: `matchProviders` and `orgNameTokens` in `lib/render/frontier.mjs` both map `aliases[].name` with a 3-character floor and nothing else. So `seed` becomes (a) a board-join key that matches any future catalog provider id containing the substring — today only `bytedance-seed`, tomorrow anything a router files under a name with `seed` in it — and (b) an ownership token, making any registrable domain whose bought label is exactly `seed` read as this organisation's own. The alias buys nothing in return, since `manual` means it is never wrapped in prose. Dropping it, or narrowing it to a form that carries the vendor name, would close both without any loss.

### Cite the three comparison likes counts, or narrow the fact to the one the URL supports

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-1.md`.

The fact `hermes_4_likes` carries "299, against 215 for Hermes-4-70B, 181 for Hermes-4-14B and 94 for Hermes-4-405B" with a single `source_url`, https://huggingface.co/api/models/NousResearch/Hermes-4.3-36B. That document contains only the 299. I fetched all four endpoints on 2026-09-06 and every number is right (Hermes-4.3-36B likes=299, Hermes-4-70B likes=215, Hermes-4-14B likes=181, Hermes-4-405B likes=94), so nothing is false — but a reader following the rendered link can check one figure in four, and the wiki spec requires a fact's source be reachable from the rendered page. Either split the comparison into per-model facts each citing its own `/api/models/...` endpoint, or reduce this fact to the 299 and move the comparison into prose that names the other three URLs.

### The portal row count does not reproduce at 332

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-2.md`.

`portal_catalog` states "332 distinct named model rows, counted from the landing page's own per-1M price cells". Fetching https://portal.nousresearch.com/ on 2026-09-06 (the fact's own `accessed` date) and extracting the embedded `{"displayName","modelName","tokenPrice"}` rows gives 346 rows, 346 distinct `modelName`, 337 distinct `displayName`, and 333 distinct `modelName` once the 13 `~`-prefixed free-tier duplicate ids are dropped. No counting convention I tried lands on 332; the nearest is 333. Same-day drift of one row is the likely explanation and this is not blocking, but the figure should either be re-counted with the convention stated ("distinct model ids, free-tier duplicates excluded") or softened. The load-bearing half of the claim is exactly right and I confirmed it: of all 346 rows, zero match /nous|hermes|nomos|consilience|psyche/ in either id or display name.

### Two launch-post quotes are classed `slow` where `dated` is what they are

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-3.md`.

`hermes_4_3_claim` ("nearly matches (and in some cases exceeds) the performance of Hermes 4 70B at half the parameter cost") and `psyche_production_first` ("our first production model post-trained entirely on the Psyche network") both carry `volatility: slow`, which the schema defines as re-check within 120 days. Both are fixed sentences in a dated launch post and cannot change; `dated` is the class the spec defines for exactly this ("true as of its date, displayed with the date, never re-checked"). As classed they will enter the overdue sweep in February for a re-check that can only confirm the same bytes. The neighbouring quote fact `psyche`, from the same kind of source, is already classed `dated`.

Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file. ### "Not one of the eight rivals is in that class" overreaches — three publish no size Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-1.md`. The body asserts "Not one of the eight rivals in its own comparison table is in that class". The entry's own transcluded `comparison_table_sizes`, rendered in the next breath, says five rivals publish a size (Tencent Hy3 295B-A21B, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-A55B, Inkling 975B-A41B, DeepSeek-V4-Pro Max 1.6T-A49B, Kimi K3 2.8T-A50B) "and Qwen 3.7 Max, Muse Spark 1.1 and Claude Fable 5 carrying an em dash where a size would go". For those three the size is undisclosed, not known-to-be-larger, so the sentence claims more than the table shows. "Not one of the five that publishes a size is in that class, and three publish none" is exact and no weaker. Carried rather than blocked because the transclusion immediately below discloses the em dashes, so the reader can see the gap. Re-filed from the pass-1 record, confirmed here against the entry's own front matter. ### Restore the vendor's hedge to the weight-class quote Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-2.md`. `weight_class_claim` quotes "the most capable agentic coding model in its weight class by a wide margin" and labels it "the vendor's own bolded comparison", which is honest and not a misquotation. But the served sentence is "Laguna S 2.1 is, as far as we can measure, the most capable agentic coding model in its weight class by a wide margin." — confirmed by fetching https://poolside.ai/blog/introducing-laguna-s-2-1 on 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 465,772 bytes) and finding "as far as we can measure" twice, once in the rendered HTML and once in the Sanity block payload as a span reading "Laguna S 2.1 is, as far as we can measure, ". Dropping that clause makes Poolside sound more absolute than it was, in a paragraph whose whole argument is about the vendor's hedging. Adding it to the fact value costs nothing. Re-filed from the pass-1 record, confirmed here by my own fetch. ### Say "repository" on the two bare parenthetical dates in the licence paragraph Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-05-carry-4.md`. The licence paragraph establishes a repository-creation frame ("Laguna XS.2's repository went up on 23 April 2026 ... Laguna M.1's on 15 June") and then drops the noun for the next two: "Laguna XS 2.1 (20 June) is openmdw-1.1 and Laguna S 2.1 (13 July) is ...". Both parentheticals are Hugging Face createdAt dates and both are correct, but a reader landing mid-paragraph reads them as release dates, and the announcements were 2 July and 21 July — dates the entry's own timeline carries three rows apart from these. Not a false claim; a dropped qualifier on a number the entry states twice under two different meanings. "XS 2.1's repository (20 June)" would close it. ### Retiring these findings These files' presence is what puts the findings in the Pulse's derived queue.
